title: General Election 1928
description: The legendary 'Cossack Election' focusing on the future welfare state, taxation, and labor market regulation.

historicalOutcome.summary: The Right (General Electoral League) achieved its greatest election victory after a fierce campaign against the Social Democrats' tax proposals. Arvid Lindman formed a conservative government with support from the Free-minded People's Party.

Q1.description: The relief work system (AK) with its low wages remained intact between 1928–1932. In the long term, it was abolished in the 1940s in favor of modern labor market policies.

Q2.description: The Collective Bargaining Act and Labor Court remained in force and later established the foundation of the 'Swedish model'.

Q3.description: The 1925 disarmament decision was not reversed. Defense policy remained locked until the major defense act of 1936.

Q4.description: The proposed inheritance tax increase was voted down in 1928, though higher wealth taxes were introduced in the post-war era.

Q5.description: Grain tariffs were introduced in the early 1930s due to the Great Depression, initiating decades of agricultural regulation.

Q6.description: Prohibition was rejected. The 'Bratt System' ration book remained in effect until 1955 when Systembolaget was created.

Q7.description: The coffee tariff was not introduced, and coffee remained an unregulated household staple.

Q8.description: State Railways (SJ) retained its position, but road infrastructure saw major expansion starting in the 1930s.

Q9.description: Civil marriage remained available, though religious wedding ceremonies remained the social norm.

Q10.description: Film censorship remained, but radio and phonographs grew into essential mass media without new entertainment taxes.

Q11.description: The eight-hour workday was maintained and served as the standard until the 40-hour work week law in 1970.

Q12.description: The 1927/1928 school reforms were a first step; the unified 9-year comprehensive school was fully implemented in 1962.

Q13.description: Local bans on public dance halls were tested, but outdoor dance pavilions exploded in popularity in folk parks.

Q14.description: Trade with the Soviet Union continued via industrial contracts without large-scale state credit guarantees.

Q15.description: Defense secrecy remained stable until World War II when military secrecy was tightened sharply.

Q16.description: Strict fiscal discipline was maintained until 1933, when a political agreement created active counter-cyclical crisis management.

questions.title: Unemployment Relief & AK Work
questions.statement: State relief work wages should strictly be kept lower than the lowest market collective agreement wage.
questions.context: The Unemployment Commission (AK) provided relief work but was criticized by unions for lowering wage levels during labor disputes.
questions.pro: Prevents passivity and limits state expenditure.
questions.con: Undermines union agreements and forces workers into poverty.

questions.title: Collective Bargaining Act
questions.statement: The new law on collective agreements and the Labor Court (prohibiting wildcat strikes) should be repealed immediately.
questions.context: Passed in 1928 despite strong opposition from labor unions who viewed it as a threat to the right to strike.
questions.pro: Restores full union autonomy and unrestricted right to strike.
questions.con: Ensures industrial peace and predictability for businesses.

questions.title: Defense Disarmament
questions.statement: Sweden should maintain the 1925 decision on major military disarmament.
questions.context: Following WWI, left and liberal parties passed major military spending cuts to redirect funds to social welfare.
questions.pro: Frees up state resources for healthcare and public education.
questions.con: Jeopardizes national security in an uncertain international climate.

questions.title: Increased Inheritance Tax
questions.statement: Inheritance tax should be raised significantly on large fortunes to fund social insurance.
questions.context: Social Democrats proposed higher wealth and inheritance taxes to finance public welfare reforms.
questions.pro: Reduces social inequality and finances social safety nets.
questions.con: Penalizes savings and drains family enterprises of capital.

questions.title: Grain Tariffs
questions.statement: Swedish agriculture should be protected against cheap grain imports through tariffs.
questions.context: During the 1920s, Swedish farmers faced falling prices caused by cheap grain imported from North America.
questions.pro: Protects domestic farmers and rural livelihoods.
questions.con: Increases bread prices for urban working-class families.

questions.title: Total Alcohol Prohibition
questions.statement: Introduce a complete ban on the manufacturing and sale of alcohol in Sweden.
questions.context: Following the close 1922 referendum, prohibition remained a key objective for temperance movements.
questions.pro: Eliminates social and medical harm caused by alcoholism.
questions.con: Infringes on individual freedom and increases bootlegging.

questions.title: Coffee Tariff
questions.statement: Import tariffs should be placed on coffee to strengthen state finances.
questions.context: Coffee was viewed by some politicians as a non-essential luxury import weakening Sweden's trade balance.
questions.pro: Generates state revenue and reduces foreign currency outflow.
questions.con: Burdens everyday households enjoying a staple beverage.

questions.title: Railways vs. Road Network
questions.statement: The state should prioritize expanding railways over roads for private automobiles.
questions.context: Automobile traffic expanded rapidly in the 1920s, challenging the state-owned railway monopoly.
questions.pro: Railways provide reliable, public transport infrastructure.
questions.con: Motorized transport represents freedom of mobility for the future.

questions.title: Civil Marriage Access
questions.statement: Civil marriage should be made accessible without requiring formal withdrawal from the State Church.
questions.context: Debates continued in the 1920s regarding secular rights versus Church authority over civil status.
questions.con: Undermines the traditional role and authority of the Church.

questions.title: Cinema Censorship & Entertainment Tax
questions.statement: Films and popular entertainment should be subject to stricter state censorship and taxes.
questions.context: The boom in cinema and gramophone records sparked public debates regarding youth culture and morality.
questions.pro: Protects youth from moral decline and raises public revenue.
questions.con: Restricts cultural freedom and increases costs for popular recreation.

questions.title: Eight-Hour Workday
questions.statement: The eight-hour workday law should be maintained without granting new exemptions for industry.
questions.context: Passed in 1919, the workday law was a major achievement for labor, but employers frequently requested exemptions.
questions.pro: Guarantees rest and leisure time for industrial workers.
questions.con: Restricts operational flexibility for seasonal agricultural and industrial work.

questions.title: Unified Six-Year Elementary School
questions.statement: Secondary grammar schools should directly build upon a unified six-year primary school.
questions.context: The 1927 school reform aimed to create a more equal public educational structure across social classes.
questions.pro: Creates an equal opportunity system based on merit rather than wealth.
questions.con: Risks lowering academic standards in secondary grammar schools.

questions.title: Municipal Ban on Open-Air Dance Halls
questions.statement: Municipalities should have the right to ban public outdoor dance halls in rural areas.
questions.context: The 'dance hall debate' pitched religious conservatives against youth gathering at outdoor pavilions.
questions.pro: Reduces public drunkenness and disorder in rural communities.
questions.con: Restricts the primary social venue for rural youth.

questions.title: Trade Relations with USSR
questions.statement: Sweden should expand state-backed commercial trade relations with the Soviet Union.
questions.context: Exporters saw Soviet demand as a key market, while conservatives strongly opposed state credit guarantees.
questions.pro: Opens a major export market for Swedish manufacturing.
questions.con: Supports a communist dictatorship and poses financial risks.

questions.title: Military Secrecy
questions.statement: Military defense reports and strategic planning should be placed under stricter secrecy.
questions.context: Military leaders sought to limit public disclosure of defense plans to prevent foreign intelligence gathering.
questions.pro: Protects national security against foreign espionage.
questions.con: Limits press freedom and democratic oversight.

questions.title: Tax-Financed State Investment
questions.statement: Public investments should be financed strictly through tax revenue rather than state borrowing.
questions.context: A debate between conservative fiscal austerity and active public spending policy.
questions.pro: Prevents the accumulation of national debt.
questions.con: Restricts essential state investments in national infrastructure.

parties.name: Electoral League (Conservatives)
parties.description: Promoted national defense, property rights, and law and order under the slogan 'Do your duty, demand your rights'.

parties.name: Free-minded People's Party (Liberals)
parties.description: Centrist party led by Prime Minister Carl Gustaf Ekman. Supported temperance, free trade, and moderate social reform.

parties.name: Farmers' League
parties.description: Agrarian party championing rural interests and agricultural tariffs to protect domestic farming.

parties.name: Social Democratic Party
parties.description: Led by Per Albin Hansson envisioning the 'People's Home'. Focused on expanding welfare security and labor rights.

parties.name: Communist Party (SKP)
parties.description: Radical working-class party advocating socialist revolution and aligned with the Comintern.
